title: Extending Service-Level Agreement configurations
notes: Assignment Ready defines when an assignment SLA starts: immediately, after a fixed delay, or at a DateTime property. Creation and readiness can differ. This setting applies to assignment SLAs; do not assume it delays every case-level deadline.

GetNextWork uses assignment urgency. Assignment urgency combines the case contribution at assignment creation, assignment SLA increments and a manual assignment adjustment, capped at 100. A later manual change to case urgency does not retroactively update an existing assignment's case contribution.
examples: A settlement task is created at 10:00 but can start only at 16:00. Store today's settlement opening time in a DateTime property and start the assignment SLA then; a two-hour deadline is 18:00.
A case contributes 20, the assignment SLA contributes 10 and a manual assignment adjustment contributes 5. The assignment priority is 35 before later SLA increments.
pitfalls: Creation is not readiness
Start the clock before the operator can work.
Configure Assignment Ready against the actual start requirement.
Case versus assignment
Changing case urgency always updates every existing assignment.
Distinguish case priority from the assignment's own SLA and adjustment.
questions: A reconciliation assignment exists at noon but cannot be processed until a daily cut-off stored on the case. Which Assignment Ready configuration fits?
Dynamically defined on a DateTime property
Immediately, with an increased urgency
A fixed delay regardless of the cut-off date
A case status field used as a duration
A DateTime property represents the actual opening time. A fixed delay cannot reliably model a variable cut-off; urgency controls priority rather than readiness.
A task must wait exactly 45 minutes after creation before its SLA begins. Which configuration is simplest?
Timed delay of 45 minutes
Goal of 45 minutes starting immediately
Deadline of 45 minutes starting immediately
Manual assignment urgency adjustment
A timed delay shifts readiness. Goal and deadline intervals measure work after the SLA starts; they do not model a wait before it starts.
An assignment becomes ready at 09:30 and its deadline is two hours after readiness. With no business-calendar adjustment, when is the deadline?
Two hours after case creation, regardless of readiness
At the next stage transition
The assignment SLA interval starts at readiness. This scenario explicitly excludes calendar adjustments.
Which TWO are supported ways to establish assignment readiness?
A DateTime property
A fixed timed delay
An Access Role name
A field-value label
Readiness can be immediate, property-driven or delayed. Authorization records and labels do not schedule the assignment SLA.
A supervisor changes case urgency after an assignment was created. Why should the existing assignment's priority be checked separately?
Its case-urgency contribution was taken at assignment creation
Assignment urgency can never change
Every existing assignment is deleted
GetNextWork uses only case urgency
Assignment SLA and assignment adjustments can change priority, but a later manual case urgency adjustment does not automatically replace the creation-time contribution.
A case contributes 15, the assignment SLA contributes 20 and the assignment adjustment is 5. What urgency follows, before any cap is needed?
These three assignment-urgency components total 40. Counting only the SLA or case contribution omits part of the calculation.
Which priority is used by GetNextWork to select the next eligible assignment?
Assignment urgency
The module's quiz score
Only the case-type label
The ruleset patch version
GetNextWork prioritizes eligible assignments using assignment urgency. This is distinct from application metadata.
An SLA escalation would raise assignment urgency beyond the supported range. Which upper bound should the design respect?
There is no upper bound
Urgency is bounded at 100. A higher number is not an unlimited priority mechanism; design escalation actions as well as increments.

title: Parallel processing
notes: Independent stage processes can run concurrently. Split Join coordinates different subprocesses; Split For Each repeats one subprocess over a page list or page group. A spinoff lets the parent continue without joining back.

Use Split For Each when each eligible list/group item needs the same subprocess. Choose a join rule deliberately: All waits for every branch; Any continues after one completes and cancels remaining open assignments. Iterate processes qualifying pages sequentially.
Split Join starts different subprocesses and resumes according to All, Any or Some join criteria. Some can express a completion count or condition; do not silently assume every branch must finish.

Subprocess configuration controls the flow, page context and parameters. Review locking when branches share a case. A subprocess invoked on an embedded page must use that page's class and data rather than an unrelated top-level context.
examples: A facilities request needs a safety assessment and a budget assessment. They are different processes and can run concurrently; the parent joins after both finish.
A delivery has a page list of packages. Run one inspection subprocess for each package and wait for All before dispatch.
Three specialist teams assess one proposal; the business needs two completed assessments. A Some join expresses the threshold.
An inspection flow runs on each Package page and receives an inspection-level parameter. Test that edits affect the intended package and that concurrent case saves are handled.
pitfalls: Repeated versus different flows
Use Split Join merely because a list has many items.
Repeat the same flow with Split For Each.
Spinoff is not a join
The parent waits for a spun-off process.
Use a joining shape when completion is a prerequisite.
questions: A shipment process launches a non-blocking stock replenishment flow and must continue immediately. Which option fits?
Subprocess with Spinoff
Split Join with All
Split For Each with All
A Wait step for replenishment completion
A spinoff does not rejoin the parent. Joining shapes and a wait would make the replenishment a completion dependency.
An application must run the same verification flow for each member of a page list. Which shape matches?
Split For Each
Split Join for unrelated flows
A single assignment without iteration
A case-level SLA
The cardinality is driven by list items while the flow stays the same. That is the Split For Each use case.
A Split For Each uses Any. One branch completes. What happens to the remaining open assignments?
They are cancelled as the parent resumes
They must all finish before the parent resumes
They become new case types
They all turn into spinoffs automatically
Any allows the first completed branch to satisfy the join and cancels remaining open assignments. It does not mean continue while all branches remain required.
A delivery cannot proceed until every package check is complete. Which join criterion expresses this?
All
Any
Spinoff
The first eligible operator
All makes every started subprocess a completion dependency. Any would allow the parent to continue too early.
Legal review and financial review are different flows that must run concurrently and both finish. Which configuration fits?
Split Join with All
Split For Each with one flow name
Spinoff for both reviews
Sequential Iterate over one embedded list
Split Join coordinates different subprocesses. All preserves the requirement that both reviews finish before continuation.
A parent may continue after two of three different assessments complete. Which join option should be considered?
Some with the required completion count
All regardless of the count
Spinoff
A ruleset validation mode
Some expresses a threshold rather than requiring all branches. The count must be configured to match the business rule.
Two parallel assignments edit the same case. Which TWO design checks are necessary?
Review the case locking strategy
Test stale-data refresh and save behavior
Disable all validation permanently
Assume parallel flows create separate database cases automatically
Parallel flow execution does not remove shared-case concurrency. Locking and stale-data handling protect the edits.
A subprocess is invoked on an embedded DeliveryItem page. What should determine its data context?
The selected step page and its class
Whichever operator opened the portal first
The highest ruleset version alone
A new unrelated clipboard page for every property
The subprocess must operate on the intended page/class and parameters. Operator timing and ruleset versions do not select the business data page.

title: Managing concurrent Case access
notes: Allow one user applies an exclusive lock when opening a case for editing. Allow multiple users permits concurrent opening and checks whether the persisted case changed when saving; a stale user must refresh. Locking protects data consistency and is separate from authorization.
examples: Two coordinators open a booking. With multiple-user locking, the first saves a new date; the second must refresh and reconcile rather than overwrite that update. Use one-user locking when a long edit must be exclusive.
pitfalls: Concurrent access is not last-writer-wins
Allow multiple users means blindly overwrite on save.
Detect intervening changes and require refresh.
Lock versus permission
A lock grants a user access to confidential data.
Configure access control independently.
questions: A claims calculation requires exclusive editing while an adjuster prepares it. Which case locking strategy fits?
Allow one user
Allow multiple users without conflict checks
Disable authorization
Use a field-value list
An exclusive edit lock prevents another editor from changing the case during that edit. Field values and authorization do not implement concurrency control.
Two agents open the same case under Allow multiple users. Agent A saves first. What should Agent B do if the saved case has changed?
Refresh and reconcile before saving
Force an unconditional overwrite
Delete Agent A's assignment
Disable the SLA
Optimistic concurrency detects stale data at save. Refreshing preserves the prior save and lets the user apply changes to current data.
Which TWO statements describe Allow multiple users?
Several users may open the case
The system checks for an intervening change before saving
All writes bypass conflict detection
Every editor receives a separate independent case automatically
Concurrent opening and save-time conflict detection are the defining behavior. The users still share one case instance.
A second operator sees that a case is locked. Does waiting for the lock establish permission to read sensitive fields?
No; authorization must still permit access
Yes; every unlocked case is public
Yes; urgency grants field access
Only if the operator has the same timezone
Locks coordinate writers. Access rules and policies determine what the operator may access.
Which failure does case locking primarily prevent?
Conflicting updates overwriting each other's data
Every connector timeout
Incorrect translations
A missing ruleset prerequisite
The locking strategy addresses concurrent changes to shared case data, not integration availability or ruleset setup.
An exclusive edit lock has expired while another operator saved. Which assumption is unsafe?
The first editor can save its old snapshot without checking
The first editor should reload current data
The edit needs a valid lock when committing
The users may need to reconcile overlapping changes
An expired lock does not reserve ownership forever. Saving stale state can overwrite another operator's work.
A case type has parallel review tasks. Which requirement favors multiple-user locking?
Reviewers need concurrent access, with save conflicts handled
Every field is confidential
A single editor must hold exclusive access for the whole task
The application has only one ruleset
Concurrent work is supported when the design accepts refresh/reconciliation. Confidentiality is a separate access-control concern.
Which test most directly validates a concurrency design?
Open the same case in two sessions, save changes and observe the second save
Run a quiz about case terminology
Change only the portal theme
Export a ruleset without opening a case
A two-session stale-save test exercises the actual lock and conflict behavior rather than only configuration metadata.

title: Flow Action processing
notes: Pre-processing runs when a Flow Action is presented or selected; post-processing runs after successful submission. Pre-processing can execute again on revisit, so defaults must not overwrite intentional edits. Prefer a Declare Expression for a value that should remain derived rather than recalculating it on each action.

Configure pre/post Data Transforms, activities or supported automations on the Flow Action's Action tab. Post-processing can save one or more savable Data Pages, with parameters and When conditions. Define persistence timing deliberately; displaying a form is not committing its external data.
examples: Populate a default meeting only when none was deliberately selected or removed. When the user revisits the form, do not recreate a deleted default.
On successful submission of a supplier form, save D_Supplier with the supplier ID parameter. Skip the save when the form represents an unchanged draft.
pitfalls: Repeated initialization
Pre-processing runs only once per case.
Make initialization safe on repeated presentation.
Derived value versus action hook
Use an activity for every calculated display field.
Prefer a declarative expression when the requirement is a dependency.
questions: A form needs default contact data before the user sees it. Which Flow Action hook is appropriate?
Pre-processing
Post-processing only
A product export
A completed-case archival job
Pre-processing prepares data before presentation. Post-processing follows a successful submission.
A user removes a suggested event, leaves the assignment, then returns. Why must the initializer be guarded?
Pre-processing may run again and recreate the removed default
Post-processing always runs when a browser tab opens
Data Transforms cannot read properties
The case must be recreated
A Flow Action can be presented repeatedly. Initialization must preserve intentional user choices, including removal of a default.
A full-name field must stay synchronized with first and last name throughout processing. Which design should be evaluated first?
Declare Expression
Post-processing activity on every unrelated action
A separate background job per keystroke
A product rule
A dependent calculated value is declarative. Tying it only to one Flow Action risks stale values outside that action.
Which event normally triggers Flow Action post-processing?
Successful submission of the Flow Action
Opening the portal homepage
Selecting a different track
Installing a ruleset
Post-processing performs wrap-up work after submission; it is not a general page-load hook.
Where are pre- and post-processing references configured for a Flow Action?
Its Action tab
Only in the operator's work group
In the ruleset password field
In the report column label
The Flow Action form's Action tab holds these hooks. Organization and report records have different purposes.
A submitted form must update an external supplier record. Which supported post-processing mechanism fits?
Save a configured savable Data Page
Change an attachment category
Modify only the displayed label
Run Assignment Ready
A savable Data Page executes its save plan against the data source. Display changes alone do not persist external records.
Which TWO can be configured for a savable Data Page used in Flow Action post-processing?
Values for Data Page parameters
A When condition controlling whether to save
The mock exam pass threshold
A blanket bypass of external authentication
Parameters identify the data to save; a When condition can make the save conditional. Authentication remains necessary.
A single Flow Action needs to commit two configured data sources after submission. Which statement is correct?
Multiple savable Data Pages can be configured as post-processing actions
Only one Data Page can ever be saved by a Flow Action
Both sources must be merged into a ruleset record
Pre-processing guarantees both saves before the form opens
Flow Action post-processing supports multiple Data Pages. The single-page restriction of an individual Save Data Page step does not impose the same restriction here.

title: Organization records
notes: Organization, division and unit describe the enterprise hierarchy; units can have children. Work groups represent operational teams that can span business units. These records support routing and reporting but do not replace access roles.

A work queue holds shared assignments; a work group associates operators, managers and queues. A worklist holds assignments for an individual operator. Match team-level routing to a queue and individual ownership to a worklist.

Maintain operator organizational membership, work group/queue associations and routing references together. Test that eligible team members can retrieve shared work and that managers can oversee the intended group; renaming an organization is not a substitute for updating routing.
examples: A retailer has an organization, regional divisions and fulfillment units. A returns work group spans fulfillment and support without changing the reporting hierarchy.
Route unclaimed returns reviews to ReturnsQueue, then let eligible operators obtain work. A named specialist's follow-up can go to that specialist's worklist.
When a new branch opens, create its unit and operators, associate them with the appropriate work group, and test queue access and escalation to the manager.
pitfalls: Hierarchy versus team
Every work group must be a division.
Use work groups for operational collaboration across units.
Queue versus list
A work queue belongs to one individual like a worklist.
A queue contains shared work; a worklist represents individual assignments.
questions: Which order describes the standard organization hierarchy?
Organization → Division → Unit
Work Queue → Ruleset → Portal
Operator → Product → Case
Worklist → Access Role → Division
Organization records model the enterprise as organization, division and unit, with possible child units.
Designers and analysts in different units collaborate on shared work. Which record models their operational team?
Work group
A new property type
A ruleset patch
A field-value rule
A work group can span organizational units and associates the operational team with shared queues and management.
An unassigned task must be available to several eligible team members. Where should it be routed?
Work queue
One operator's personal worklist regardless of availability
The application definition
A clipboard-only list with no assignment
A work queue holds shared assignments. A personal worklist would give the task individual ownership.
A task is explicitly assigned to one specialist. Which container represents that person's assignments?
Worklist
The ruleset stack
An attachment category
A node classification
A worklist holds assignments for an individual operator; work queues hold shared work.
Which TWO belong to work group configuration concerns?
The team's manager
Associated shared work queues
Every SQL query's index
The application product archive checksum
A work group connects team members, management and shared queues. Database tuning and package integrity are separate concerns.
An operator moves to a new team but sees no shared tasks. Which configuration should be checked first?
Operator work group and queue associations
The browser's text color
The mock exam name
The ruleset's patch count alone
Membership and queue associations determine the operational work available to the operator. Visual settings do not route work.
A new unit is created. Which test best validates the accompanying routing change?
Create a case and verify its assignment reaches the intended queue or operator
Check only that the unit label renders
Export every ruleset
Increase all case urgency to 100
The actual assignment destination validates routing. A visible organizational record does not prove the routing references are correct.
Does placing an operator in a division alone establish all application permissions?
No; access groups, roles and policies still govern authorization
Yes; every division grants full developer access
Yes; divisions replace authentication
Only if the work queue is empty
Organization membership can inform routing and authorization logic, but it is not a universal replacement for access-control configuration.
